about: Cases for the private assistant itself (Claude), not for the rule-based reader. Each turn has what the person says and `model`: what a careful model would return for it. Tests replay `model` through the real code path, so they check everything code does with a model's answer. `npm run sim:extract -- --llm` ignores `model`, asks the real model instead, and compares what ends up stored with `expected`. Paths in `expected` and `absent` are dotted paths into the stored member state.

cases.note: Class until 6:30 is never said as a time preference, but it means no start before 7 PM.

turns.user: I have class until 6:30 that day

model.reply: Got it, nothing before 6:30 PM for you. Is there anything you can't eat?

cases.note: A wish, not a limit: recorded as an ideal with the default strength, and no ceiling.

turns.user: I'd like to keep it around $30 if we can

model.reply: Around $30 a person, noted. How far would you be willing to travel?

cases.note: A stated limit: a ceiling, strength must.

turns.user: I can't spend more than $40

model.reply: I'll try hard to keep it under $40 a person. What time works for you?

cases.note: Says it matters a lot, without making it a condition.

turns.user: I'm really hoping for Korean food

model.reply: Korean it is, and I've marked that it matters to you. What time works for you?

cases.note: Saying two meals work rules nothing out; dinner is a mild wish. Meal hours come from code.

turns.user: Lunch or dinner both work for me, dinner would be a bit nicer

model.reply: Lunch or dinner, with dinner preferred. Is there anything you can't eat?

cases.about: don't mind leaves a field out
cases.note: "I don't mind" answers the travel question that was just asked. Nothing is recorded for travel, and it is not asked again.

model.reply: Dinner, got it. How long a trip would you be OK with?

turns.user: Honestly I don't mind

model.reply: No limit on distance then. Is there anything you can't eat?

cases.note: An allergy cannot be checked against restaurants: it is a private note, not a constraint, and it answers the cannot-eat question.

turns.user: I'm allergic to peanuts

model.reply: I've noted the peanut allergy for you. I can't check restaurants for it, so please look at the menu. What time works for you?

cases.note: Vegetarian can be checked; spicy cannot and becomes a note; seafood becomes a kind of place to leave out.

turns.user: I'm vegetarian, and I can't do spicy food or seafood

model.reply: Vegetarian, and no seafood places. I've noted no spicy food for you, but I can't check restaurants for that. What time works for you?

cases.note: The name is kept as typed and matched by code. A place that is not a candidate yet is kept by name with no id; it is matched again when the plan's pool is complete.

turns.user: Could we go to ramen nagi? Just not Sizzler

model.reply: Ramen Nagi is on your wish list, and Sizzler is off it. What time works for you?

cases.about: vague budget, then a concrete answer
cases.note: A vague answer gets one concrete follow-up; the numbers arrive in the next message and the limit is a must.

turns.user: Nothing too expensive please

model.reply: Sure. What amount would feel comfortable per person, and what's the most you'd go to? It stays private.

turns.user: 30 would be nice, 50 at the very most

model.reply: Around $30, and I'll try hard to keep it under $50. What time works for you?

cases.note: An order of importance and a kind of place are recorded only because the person brought them up.

turns.user: Price matters most to me, then how far it is. And no fast food please

model.reply: Price first, then distance, and no fast food. What would you like to spend per person? It stays private.

cases.note: Issue #62. The model passes "Asian" on as a word; the table in code says what it covers, the reply says so, and nothing else in the message is lost. A favourite named afterwards scores 1 and the rest of the broad wish stays wanted, lower.

model.reply: Asian food, and I'll try hard to keep it under $40 a person. Is there a favourite among them?
